Get started

Set up GitHub, choose your agent features, and open your first repository.

About ByteQuay

ByteQuay is a macOS app for GitHub reviews and local coding agents. A workspace holds a repository’s work; a task is an agent conversation with its own working copy. App data stays on your Mac.

ByteQuay is pre-1.0. These guides follow the development version; check your release notes.

Get started

  1. Download ByteQuay from GitHub Releases and drag it to Applications. It needs macOS 14+ and includes Java.
  2. Follow the setup guide to connect GitHub and, if you like, an agent.
  3. Choose Home → Repos you watch → + Watch and pick a repository.
  4. Open Pull requests, select a PR, and inspect WorkBench → Changes.

Choose your setup

  1. GitHub: choose Use my GitHub CLI login after gh auth login, or Connect with token → with a classic token that has repo and read:user.
  2. Agent: sign in to Codex or Claude Code, or add a DeepSeek API key, then pick the Development model. Review follows it unless you change it.
  3. Automation: choose how far new tasks go, from a local commit to a merged PR. New installations start at Auto-Commit.
  4. Features: turn on Today or the Assistant if you want them. Both use your Development model allowance.

You can skip the agent and still work with GitHub and PRs. To revisit setup, choose Settings → General → Setup guide → Open setup.

Home and workspaces

Home shows your work, what others ask of you, and activity from people you follow. A workspace holds a repository’s tasks, PRs, work items, commits, and memory.

  • My work sorts your issues, tickets, tasks, and PRs into In progress, In review, Needs you, and Ready to merge. All my work lists everything, including finished work.
  • Needs attention shows up to five review requests, re-reviews, and mentions. Snooze hides one until the time you pick.
  • Approved by me lists open PRs you approved. A new review request brings one back for review.
  • Add a workspace as a Direct clone or Personal fork. Unwatch keeps local history; Delete local data removes it.

Plan the day with Today

Turn on Today in setup or Settings → Agents → Features. On working days it lists up to five things worth doing first, each with a reason. Making the list uses a model session; it never writes to GitHub or starts a task on its own.

  • Click a row for its reason and action. Done or Tomorrow sets it aside.
  • Start task starts suggested work with your saved automation.
  • On the last working day, This week looks back at what merged and slipped.
